chapter: Clarinet teachers and the Baton Rouge scene
title: Fritz's technique and why George Lewis raved about him
summary: Fritz was wiry and quiet, with technique and tone Joe admired alongside Jimmie Noone, and Joe could hear it even as a child.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: He was a kind of wiry looking guy. I would say he was a guy who would remind you of Pops Foster, the bass player. Very quiet. And they had another good clarinet player in Baton Rouge whose name was Green; I can't think of his first name.

Let me ask you a question that probably you won't know the answer to. When I interviewed George Lewis, he used to rave on and on about Isadore Fritz. He had two main... Isadore Fritz never taught George Lewis anything that George told me about anyway, but he had him and a guy called George Boyd. Why do you think George Lewis would have raved about Isadore Fritz? What would have affected a mentality like George?
His technique. Even when I was a little kid, I could understand the technique that Fritz had.
When you talk about technique, do you mean actually knowing what he was doing on the horn, or facility?
By the way he played and the tone. I could tell in those days. Fritz and Jimmie Noone was two of my favorite players in those days.
